commits.message:
fix(highlighter): style every JSON token as Rich's JSONHighlighter does (rich-json-0yq)

JSONHighlighter styled a string only when a colon came before it, so
strings inside arrays printed unstyled, and its string pattern stopped
at an escaped quote. Each token kind ran as its own pass, so `true` and
`12` inside a string were restyled as a boolean and a number.

It is now Python Rich 9d8f9a3's highlighter: one alternation of brace,
true, false, null, number and string, scanned once, then a pass that
marks each string a colon follows as a key. The theme replaces json.bool
with Rich's json.bool_true (italic bright_green) and json.bool_false
(italic bright_red). json.number becomes bold, and json.number and
json.str carry Rich's not-italic and not-bold overrides.

For the ticket's evidence calls, printJson now writes Rich's bytes apart
from SGR parameter order, which is rich-color-7kv.

fix(style): write no SGR parameter for an attribute set false (rich-style-h93)

Style.toSgrCodes wrote an attribute's off code (22, 23, ...) when the
attribute was set false. Python Rich 9d8f9a3 writes a parameter only for
an attribute set true. There, a false attribute overrides an inherited
one when styles combine. Every run is written after a reset, so the off
code never changed what a terminal shows, only the bytes: repr.url came
out as 94;23;4 where Rich writes 4;94.

This also unblocks rich-json-0yq, whose json.number and json.str styles
carry Rich's italic=False and bold=False.

fix(console): delegate printJson to the JSON renderable (rich-json-dxs.1, rich-json-dxs.2) (#116)

`Console.printJson` built a key-sorted object and passed it to
`JSON.stringify` as the replacer, behind an `as unknown as undefined`
cast. JSON.stringify ignores a plain object in that position, so
`sortKeys` did nothing, and no highlighter ran. `JSONRenderable` already
did both.

printJson now builds a `JSONRenderable` and prints it with soft wrap, as
Rich's print_json does, so a line wider than the console stays whole and
the output stays valid JSON. Its options are `JSONOptions`, which adds
`highlight`.

json.ts moves from renderables/ to core/. An import from core/console.ts
into renderables/ would have been a third upward edge out of core. The
module imports only core primitives and sits at tier 6 beside pretty, for
the reason pretty.ts's header gives. CLAUDE.md's tier list names it.

The printJson tests expect Python Rich 9d8f9a3's output for key sorting
at every depth and for a line wider than the console, and assert the
theme style Rich gives braces, keys and strings. All three fail against
the old implementation. docs/console.md no longer says printJson does
not colorize.
